title: Mughal Economy Inland Trade
definition: The complex network of internal exchange of agricultural produce, manufactured goods, and luxury items facilitated by a sophisticated system of markets (mandis/hats), merchant guilds, and state-regulated transit duties during the 16th-18th century.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the transition from a feudal to a proto-capitalist economy, the role of the merchant class (Banias/Seths), and the impact of Mughal administrative policies on regional economic integration.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Mughal Economy Inland Trade.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
